title: A JSON `null` body crashes staff-admin with an unhandled TypeError instead of BAD_JSON
claim: The body is parsed with a bare `JSON.parse(text)` and then dereferenced at `switch (body.action)` (line 69). Only the parse sits inside the try/catch. `admin.ts:148` guards the same case explicitly (`typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)`), but staff-admin does not. `JSON.parse('null')` returns null, so `body.action` throws a TypeError outside any try. Deno.serve then answers a plain-text 500 that does not follow the `{ok:false,error:{code,message}}` contract from `_shared/http.ts`. Only an active owner with a fresh TOTP can reach this, so the blast radius is small.
failure_scenario: An owner-authenticated client (or a script holding an owner token) POSTs the body `null`. Auth passes, `JSON.parse('null')` gives `null`, and `body.action` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`. The reply is Deno's default 500 with no JSON body. `TeamView.callStaffAdmin` cannot read an `error` object from it and shows the generic 'تعذّر الاتصال بالخادم.', where BAD_JSON was intended.
suggested_fix: Reuse the shape guard from admin.ts. After `body = JSON.parse(text)`, throw when `typeof body !== 'object' || body === null || Array.isArray(body)` so the existing catch answers 400 BAD_JSON.

title: Settings status reports analytics as configured when fetchAnalytics treats it as NOT_CONFIGURED
claim: `settingsStatus().analytics` is true when `ANALYTICS_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID` are set. `fetchAnalytics` (analytics.ts:216-227) also needs `SITE_URL` to parse as a URL with a non-empty host, and otherwise returns `{status:'unavailable', reason:'NOT_CONFIGURED'}`. The owner's Settings screen (SettingsView.tsx:174) prints «الإحصاءات: مضبوط» while the stats page shows the feature as not configured. The status action exists to answer whether a feature is configured, and here it gives a wrong yes.
failure_scenario: The hosted project sets ANALYTICS_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID, but SITE_URL is typed without a scheme (`anas.studio`) or is missing. `new URL('anas.studio')` throws, so `siteHost` is '' and the Settings line reads «الموقع: غير مضبوط». The next line still reads «الإحصاءات: مضبوط», while /admin/stats shows analytics unavailable (NOT_CONFIGURED). The owner is told the setup is complete when it is not.
suggested_fix: Compute `analytics` with the same gate as fetchAnalytics: `optionalEnv('ANALYTICS_TOKEN') !== undefined && optionalEnv('CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID') !== undefined && siteHost !== ''`.

title: A transient Storage read error is reported as MISSING_PART and triggers cleanup of parts that were uploaded
claim: `MediaStore.read` returns null for any `download` error, not only a missing object. `mediaComplete` treats null as 'a part was never uploaded': it runs `cleanupPrivate()` and answers 422 MISSING_PART «لم يُرفع كل جزء من الصورة.». The ticket was already claimed (once only), so the browser cannot retry the completion. A Storage 5xx during the read therefore deletes a complete upload and blames the user's upload, when the fault is server-side. The wrong-cause message, and the 422 instead of a retryable 5xx, is the defect.
failure_scenario: An editor uploads an original plus four derivatives, and all five parts are present. `media-complete` claims the ticket, then `download(stagedOriginal)` fails with a Storage 503 or a network reset. `read` returns null, so the handler calls `cleanupPrivate()` and returns 422 MISSING_PART. The parts are deleted, the ticket is spent, and the UI tells the user the upload was incomplete. The user must re-upload up to 31 MiB and cannot tell that it was a server error.
suggested_fix: Return null only when the Storage error is a not-found (check `error.statusCode`/`status` 404 or the 'not found' message). Otherwise throw, so the existing catch answers 500 FAILED «تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.».

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: Top-paths query takes 100 leading groups before the asset filter, so real pages fall out of the list
claim: `TOP_PATHS_QUERY` asks Cloudflare for the 100 highest-count `clientRequestPath` groups. The JS filter (`isRealPage`) then drops `/_next`, `/admin`, `/api` and static extensions. The 100-group cap therefore applies to assets and pages together. The constant's own comment says this: 'Top paths are taken after filtering, from this many leading groups'. The status filter added for S07.1 removes 404s and 304s but not assets. On the export that ships today the static asset URLs greatly outnumber the pages. `out/` has 197 .webp, 13 .mp4, 7 .woff2, 54 `_next` files and 212 RSC .txt payloads, against 22 public HTML pages. Shared chunks, fonts and layout images are requested about once per cold visit. Each page's own images and chunk tie or beat that page's HTML count. The 100 slots fill with assets, so only a handful of real pages survive to `parseTopPaths`. The unit test 'parseTopPaths drops assets ... then takes the top 10' feeds pre-windowed fixtures, so it cannot catch this.
failure_scenario: In the 7-day window, 60 or more shared asset URLs (chunks, the 7 fonts, layout images) each have count near the number of cold visits. Each popular page also has 10 to 20 own image and RSC URLs with counts at or above the page's HTML count. The top 100 groups by `count_DESC` are almost all assets. `parseTopPaths` filters them out and returns only 3 to 5 pages. The owner's 'أكثر الصفحات طلبًا' list omits pages that really ranked 5th to 10th, or shows fewer than 10 rows.
suggested_fix: Filter pages server-side so the window holds only pages, for example `edgeResponseContentTypeName: "html"` in the query filter (confirm the field name in the schema at gate E11). Otherwise raise `limit` to the node's maxPageSize (10000) so the JS filter sees every path. Add a test where more than 100 asset groups outrank the pages.

title: Operator-side Turnstile failures are reported to visitors as 'you are not human' with no log, so a wrong secret looks like every visitor failing the challenge
claim: verifyTurnstile discards the siteverify `error-codes` array. Any `success !== true` becomes INVALID_TOKEN, and TEST_SECRET_IN_PRODUCTION (line 56) is a non-UNREACHABLE code too. contact.ts (lines 136-139) and checkout.ts (324-326) map every code except UNREACHABLE to HTTP 400 'TURNSTILE' with the message 'تعذّر التحقق من أنك إنسان.'. Server-side causes (`invalid-input-secret`, `missing-input-secret`, `internal-error`, a test secret on a hosted site) are then indistinguishable from a bad visitor token. The visitor is told the failure is theirs, the widget resets, and every retry fails the same way. The function logs nothing, so the operator has no signal (SettingsView shows only 'configured' and 'test secret').
quote: if (typeof verified !== 'object' || verified === null || verified.success !== true) {
failure_scenario: At the first hosted deploy TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is pasted with a typo, or the secret belongs to a different widget. Cloudflare answers {success:false,'error-codes':['invalid-input-secret']}. Every contact and checkout attempt returns 400 with 'تعذّر التحقق من أنك إنسان.'. Real customers conclude they are being flagged as bots, and the checkout and contact form are dead while function logs show nothing. Cloudflare's transient `internal-error` gives the same visitor-blaming reply instead of a 503 retry.
suggested_fix: Read result['error-codes']. Map invalid-input-secret, missing-input-secret, internal-error and TEST_SECRET_IN_PRODUCTION to a server-side code that callers answer 503 TURNSTILE_UNAVAILABLE. console.warn the codes only (no token, no IP). Keep invalid-input-response and timeout-or-duplicate as INVALID_TOKEN.

title: Quota-held contact notices are recorded as an 'ok' run, so the owner home shows no warning; a contact flood then delays real notices by days
claim: After S04.1, once 80 outbox sends are used in a UTC day (or 100, or 3,000 in the month) every priority-1 contact notice waits. Those rows stay 'due' (pending, next_at <= now()), so outbox_kick() calls the function every minute. Each call claims nothing, and line 182 maps `claimed === 0` to status 'ok', so job_run_record writes a fresh 'ok' run each minute. AdminHome.emailWaiting() warns only when a row has been due for over 10 minutes AND no run finished in the last 10 minutes. The run written a minute ago defeats that rule, so the owner home reports the email job as healthy while notices are held. outbox_attention() lists only exhausted/uncertain/suppressed/bad-delivery rows, not pending ones. The scheduler-liveness signal cannot see held-back mail. On top of that, outbox_claim orders by priority, next_at, id (strict FIFO), and contact_submit queues one notice per active owner/operations member while allowing 200 messages/day (contact:all). The reserve caps notice sends at 80/day. docs/operations.md accepts the flood risk because 'nothing is lost - messages already stored still reach the owner's mailbox' and reasons only about a one-day form lockout. With the reserve, the backlog is not one day long. It is measured in days, and D31 makes the notice email the only inbox (public.contacts has no reader).
failure_scenario: Owner + one operations member are active (2 recipients). An attacker who passes Turnstile submits 200 messages in a UTC day (about 40 IPs at 5/hour, or one IP plus rotating emails). This queues 400 notice rows, 80 are sent that day, 320 stay pending. The next day another 200 arrive and the drain is 80 again, so the queue only grows. A real visitor's message stored on day 2 has its notice behind 300+ spam rows and is emailed days later, or never while the flood lasts. Meanwhile each minute's run is recorded 'ok' with claimed 0, AdminHome shows 'ok (time)' for إرسال البريد, and outbox_attention is empty. Nothing tells the owner a real message is waiting. The same silent state occurs when the 3,000/month cap is reached.
suggested_fix: Report held-back work: when claimed === 0 and outbox_due_since() is non-null (or the claim returned nothing because of the daily/reserve/monthly caps), record status 'partial' with reason 'QUOTA_HELD' and have emailWaiting/JOB_STALE_TEXT treat it as trouble. Reduce the flood's effect: lower contact:all so cap x recipients <= DAILY_QUOTA - RESERVE, or collapse notices into a digest once the day's notice budget is spent. Correct the accepted-risk paragraph in docs/operations.md.

title: S07.6 fixed only for the staff-row lookup; a transient Auth failure in getClaims is still reported as 401 UNAUTHENTICATED
claim: S07.6's root cause is "a server fault is reported as unauthenticated", so a caller such as StatsView.tsx:53 (which maps UNAUTHENTICATED to the 'forbidden' owners-only message) shows the wrong page. The fix throws for the failed staff query but leaves the sibling path in the same function. In supabase-js getClaims, any AuthError is returned as { data: null, error } rather than thrown. That includes AuthRetryableFetchError from a network failure or a 5xx from Auth, whether raised by the JWKS fetch or by the getUser fallback used for HS-signed tokens. Line 36 folds every such error into return null. Both admin.ts and staff-admin then answer 401 UNAUTHENTICATED for a valid token during an Auth blip.
failure_scenario: The owner opens the stats page while Supabase Auth answers 503. getClaims returns { error: AuthRetryableFetchError }. staffFromRequest returns null. handleAdmin replies 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. StatsView.tsx:53 maps that to 'forbidden', and the owner is shown the owners-only message. TeamView shows 'سجّل الدخول أولًا' and pushes a needless re-login. The actual state is a temporary server fault on a valid session.
suggested_fix: Import isAuthRetryableFetchError from @supabase/supabase-js. When error is set and isAuthRetryableFetchError(error) is true, throw new Error('AUTH_UNAVAILABLE') so handleAdmin and staff-admin answer 500 FAILED, and keep return null only for a genuinely invalid or expired token.

title: The 2xx-only filter also drops 304 revalidations, so repeat visits vanish from 'most requested pages'
claim: S07.1 filters top paths to edgeResponseStatus in [200, 300) to remove 404 scans and redirects. Cloudflare Pages serves the static HTML with no cache override (public/_headers sets Cache-Control only for /admin, /_next/static and similar). Pages' default for HTML is a must-revalidate policy with an ETag, so a returning visitor's browser sends a conditional request and the edge answers 304. A 304 has edgeResponseStatus 304, which the new filter excludes, so every repeat page view is missing from the count. The ranking then reflects first visits and hard reloads, and it can reorder the owner's list.
failure_scenario: /journal/riyadh-notes is read 40 times by 10 first-time visitors and 30 returning ones. The 30 returning views are 304s and are not counted, so it shows 10. /store, read 15 times by first-time visitors, shows 15 and ranks above it. The owner's list misranks the pages people actually come back to.
suggested_fix: Count 200 and 304 only. Replace the two range filters with edgeResponseStatus_in: [200, 304] (or an OR of the two statuses). Redirects (3xx other than 304), 404 and 5xx stay excluded.

verdict: split (verify first; fix only if real)
title: Per-IP throttles key on the full IPv6 address, so one /64 gets unlimited buckets
claim: requestIp returns the client address unchanged and clientKeyHash hashes that whole string. A single IPv6 subscriber or VPS controls a whole /64 (2^64 addresses), so every request can present a new address and land in a fresh finance.rate_limits row. The public `quote` action has no Turnstile, so its 300-an-hour per-IP cap (`checkout-quote:ip`) is its only throttle. The 5-an-hour contact cap and the 10-an-hour checkout cap are also per address, though they sit behind Turnstile.
failure_scenario: A script on a /64 sends `quote` requests, each from a random host address. The per-IP limit never trips. Every call runs checkout_price and inserts a new (bucket, key_hash, window_start) row. A sustained few hundred requests a second adds tens of millions of rows within the 2-day purge window (rate-limits-purge, 03:17 daily), and it burns Edge Function invocations and database CPU with no per-caller brake.
suggested_fix: In requestIp, reduce an IPv6 address to its /64 prefix (first four hextets, after IPv4-mapped normalisation) before hashing, and cap total keys per bucket per window or add Turnstile to `quote` when the caller's bucket is new.

title: A JSON `null` body crashes staff-admin with a bare 500 and no error envelope
claim: `JSON.parse(text)` is assigned to `body: Record<string, unknown>` with no object check. `admin.ts:147-149` rejects non-objects with 400 BAD_JSON, but this function does not. The body `null` passes the size check, then `body.action` at line 69 throws a TypeError outside any try/catch. `Deno.serve` answers a plain-text 500 with no CORS headers and no `{ok:false,error,requestId}` envelope, which breaks the contract `http.ts` declares for every Edge Function.
failure_scenario: An owner with a fresh TOTP (or a script holding their token) POSTs the body `null` to /functions/v1/staff-admin. JSON.parse returns null, line 69 `switch (body.action)` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`, and the reply is 500 text/plain. The browser treats it as a network/CORS failure, and TeamView shows «تعذّر الاتصال بالخادم.» instead of BAD_JSON. The same body to `admin` gets a proper 400 envelope.
suggested_fix: Reuse the `admin.ts:147-149` guard: after parsing, `if (typeof parsed !== 'object' || parsed === null || Array.isArray(parsed)) throw new Error('shape')` inside the existing try, so it returns 400 BAD_JSON.

title: Invite rollback ignores a failed deleteUser, leaving an orphaned auth user that blocks re-inviting the email
claim: When the `staff` insert fails after `createUser`, the code calls `deleteUser` and discards its `{error}` result (auth-js returns it rather than throwing). If the delete also fails, the confirmed auth user stays with no `staff` row. Every retry then hits `error?.code === 'email_exists'` and answers 409 USER_EXISTS «هذا البريد مسجّل مسبقًا.». `staff_directory` lists only `staff` rows, so the owner cannot see or remove the orphan from /admin/team.
failure_scenario: The database or GoTrue has a brief outage during an invite: `admin.from('staff').insert` returns an error, and `deleteUser` fails for the same reason. The owner sees «تعذّرت الدعوة» and retries. Every later attempt for that address returns USER_EXISTS, and only the Supabase dashboard can fix it.
suggested_fix: Check the `deleteUser` result and report it in the audit summary. Better, on `email_exists` look the user up by id, and if it has no `staff` row, insert the `staff` row for the existing id instead of answering USER_EXISTS.
